topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing for the lecture series, detailing the scope of cancer biology, student backgrounds, and specific learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer: Genetic alterations and failure of differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental conceptual view of cancer as a breakdown in normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the diagnostic, gross, and histological distinction between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of invasion, metastatic spread, and stepwise adenoma-to-adenocarcinoma progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the naming rules used to categorize benign and malignant neoplasms across tissues and explain the direct physiological mechanisms through which tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer epidemiology in human populations and across diverse animal species, framing cancer as an inherent vulnerability of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical applications of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological foundations, and comparative efficacy of screening strategies across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing, reiterating learning outcomes and offering housekeeping reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
